resources.string: Shows an ongoing notification with a short overview of what your loop is doing
Scan the barcode of a food, check the carbs for the portion you eat, then write it to a blank NFC card. Tap the card later to add the food to a meal.
Product not found. Enter the name and carbs from the package.
Could not look up the product (%1$s). Enter the name and carbs from the package.
The barcode scanner could not start (%1$s).

string.name: meal_card_per_100g
string.comment: %1$.1f=grams of carbs. Example: 67.0 g carbs per 100 g

string.name: meal_card_serving
string.comment: %1$s=serving size as written on the package. Example: Serving: 30 g (2 biscuits)

string.name: meal_card_portion_serving
string.comment: %1$.0f=serving size in grams. Example: Per serving (30 g)

string.name: meal_card_protein_fat
string.comment: %1$.1f=protein grams, %2$.1f=fat grams. Example: Protein 4.0 g, fat 2.0 g

resources.string: These values come from Open Food Facts, a database filled in by volunteers. Check them against the package before you write the card.
Hold a blank NFC card to the back of the phone.

string.name: meal_card_written
string.comment: %1$s=food name, %2$d=carbs in grams. Example: Card written: Toast, 15 g carbs

resources.string: NFC is turned off. Turn it on in the phone settings and try again.
This card is locked and cannot be written.
This card is too small. Use a shorter name or a bigger card.
This card type is not supported. Use an NTAG213 or similar card.
Writing failed. Hold the card still and try again.

Tap NFC cards with food on them to collect a meal, then open the bolus wizard with the total carbs. It never doses: you check and confirm in the wizard as usual. Card link: aaps://food?name=Toast&carbs=15&protein=4&fat=2
